settings.title: Based on clinical research
settings.body:
Compression, lateral stabilization, and patellar support are approaches that have been studied in clinical trials:

PLOS One Netzwerk-Meta-Analyse (2025) — Analysis of 139 randomized controlled trials. Knee braces were identified as the most effective type of intervention for reducing symptoms in knee osteoarthritis.

Ayık et al. (2025) — A randomized study involving 60 patients. Knee braces with lateral stabilizers improved balance and reduced pain in patients with knee osteoarthritis immediately after application.

Patella Pro Studie, BMC (2014) — A multicenter randomized trial involving 156 patients. Medial patellar stabilization as a clinically evaluated approach for anterior knee pain.

The studies refer to the method (compression, stabilization, and patellar support), not to this specific product.

settings.heading: When every step becomes uncomfortable
settings.body:
At first, it’s often just a slight tugging sensation.

Then come the moments when you suddenly feel your knee more acutely:

  • Standing up
  • On stairs
  • Sitting for a long time
  • Walking or standing for extended periods

Many people automatically start to avoid certain movements. They walk more slowly, unconsciously take the weight off their knee, or feel unsteady during everyday movements.

The problem is this: the more carefully you move, the more your knee becomes the focus of your daily life.

settings.heading: Maybe it's not just wear and tear
settings.body:
Many conventional explanations focus solely on “wear and tear.”

However, knee pain often feels more like pressure, irritation, or instability.

One possible cause may be irritated synovial tissue—the sensitive lining of the knee joint. When this tissue becomes irritated, the knee may react more sensitively to stress.

This can manifest as:

  • A feeling of pressure around the kneecap
  • Stiffness after periods of rest
  • Uncertainty during movement
  • Sensitivity under stress

Many conventional knee braces attempt to solve the problem with rigid stability. However, hard braces can be uncomfortable, slip out of place, or restrict natural movement.

That is exactly why Peakflex was designed differently.

settings.heading: Support for active knees
settings.body:
The PeakFlex knee sleeve combines multiple functions into a flexible support system for everyday use.

Instead of a heavy orthosis, you get:

  • Customizable compression
  • Lateral stabilization
  • Patella gel pads for pressure relief
  • Non-slip grip during movement

The goal is not to rigidly immobilize your knee.

PeakFlex was designed to provide comfortable support for your knee during everyday activities—whether you’re walking, working, shopping, or on the go.

settings.q: Is the PeakFlex Knee Sleeve suitable for everyday use?
settings.a: Yes. The PeakFlex Knee Sleeve was specifically designed for everyday activities such as walking, working, climbing stairs, or standing for long periods of time.

settings.q: Can I adjust the compression myself?
settings.a: Yes. With the built-in precision dial, you can adjust the compression to your liking—depending on how much support feels comfortable.

settings.q: Does the sleeve slip when you walk?
settings.a: The PeakFlex Knee Sleeve features a non-slip silicone grip designed to help reduce slipping and rolling.

settings.q: Can I wear the sleeve under my clothes?
settings.a: Yes. Its flexible and compact design ensures that the bandage can be worn comfortably under most everyday clothing.

settings.q: Is the knee brace suitable for both knees?
settings.a: Yes. The PeakFlex Knee Sleeve can be worn on either the left or right knee.

settings.q: Can I wear the sleeve for longer?
settings.a: The bandage was designed for everyday use. Many customers wear it while working, going for walks, or doing everyday activities.
